long_biography.plain_text:
Investment analyst Jason Pilalas collected objects that preserved the stories of the Royal Navy. His acquisitions ranged from hundreds of ships' bells to paintings, nameplates and medals. An auction of a naval officer's collection drew him into medal collecting; he spent the next twenty-seven years seeking examples from around the world.

With his wife, Rena, he donated an engraved pocket watch to the National Museum of Bermuda. He had bought it at auction because of its naval and island connections. The watch had been given to a seaman who rescued a captain from drowning, preserving a personal record of the rescue and the family's gratitude.
